svg.title: Five compliance requirements mapped to network design elements and to the evidence an auditor will ask for
svg.desc: Encryption in transit means IPsec or TLS on public links and a decision on internal links from data classification, evidenced by a link inventory and cipher configuration. Least-privilege access means the cardholder data environment is segmented and every cross-domain flow passes a stateful device, evidenced by a segment diagram and a rule export. Log retention means a dedicated log segment, one-way export and a single time source, evidenced by retention settings and an immutability proof. Data residency means an in-country instance with one-way de-identified flow and local collection points. Auditable third-party access means a dedicated supplier channel with per-ticket access and session recording.
svg.text: Compliance clauses are requirements; design needs constraints
Each row below is one clause, the element it forces into the design, and the artefact that proves it later
REQUIREMENT
WHAT IT FORCES INTO THE DESIGN
WHAT PROVES IT AFTERWARDS
encryption in transit
PCI DSS requirement 4
Public links must be IPsec or TLS. Internal links are decided
by data classification — MACsec where the data says so
Link inventory with the protocol per link; cipher
configuration; key rotation record
least-privilege access
PCI DSS requirement 7
The cardholder data environment is separately segmented
(VLAN or VRF); every cross-domain flow passes a stateful device
Segment diagram the assessor can walk; rule export;
periodic review minutes with names on them
log retention and immutability
PCI DSS 10 · GDPR
A dedicated log segment, one-way export, and a single
NTP source — logs with the wrong time have no evidentiary value
Retention setting; write-once or hash proof; the time
source and a sample query run in front of the auditor
data residency
data sovereignty
In-country instance, one-way de-identified flow, local storage —
including the monitoring collection points, which are stores too
Data flow diagram; egress rule set; proof that the collector
and the backup sit inside the border as well
auditable third-party access
HIPAA · GDPR
Suppliers come through a dedicated channel, access is opened
per ticket and time-boxed, sessions are recorded and audited
Ticket-to-session mapping, recording samples, and the
expiry that closed the access without anyone asking
The deliverable is an evidence chain, not a control list
Auditors do not inspect what you configured; they test whether you can show it was that way at any point in time.
Logs, time synchronisation, change records and periodic review are design outputs, handed over with the network design.
A design that cannot produce these five artefacts is not non-compliant yet — it is unauditable, which fails the same way and later.
